what: 6 screens at 1280 (run 10's inventory, learning, clinic; analytics, billing, crm): designed, shadow, quiet, the wide title at 28 (title), all three (all).
judges: Judges: Opus and Sonnet subagents of a Claude Code session, shown the versions unlabeled and shuffled (ways.py pack); not judge.py, because no API key was at hand.

judgments.why: B and D give the page title a stronger bold weight that anchors the hierarchy, while A, C and E use a weaker title; all share the misaligned, heavier-shadowed bottom cards.
B and D have a bolder, larger page title giving clearer hierarchy; the others are otherwise near-identical with a weak title.

A and B use a bold, larger page title that sets a clear hierarchy over the section cards, while C, D and E have a weak regular-weight title; layouts are otherwise identical, including the cramped plan toggle.
A and B have a larger bold page title with clearer hierarchy; C, D, E are otherwise identical with a weaker title.

C combines the strongest page title, subtle card elevation and a full-width Manage rooms button that anchors the side card, while the others each miss one or more of these (A has a weak title and a stubby button).
C pairs the larger bold title with a full-width Manage rooms button and soft card shadow; B has the big title but a small button; D/E have the full-width button with a weaker title; A has neither.

All share a broken, empty contact detail panel (blank name, $0, stray comma), so B edges ahead only through its bold page title plus soft table elevation, with C close behind and D the flattest and weakest.
All share a broken, empty detail panel; B and C have the stronger page title, and B adds the table shadow and a narrower search that avoids truncation.
A pairs a bold, confident page title with soft card elevation for the clearest hierarchy; D has the title but flatter cards, C and E the elevation but a weak title, and B lacks both.
A combines a larger bold title with soft card shadows for depth; D has the title but flat cards; C and E have shadows but a small title; B has neither.
D combines a bold page title, soft card elevation and a full-width Open calendar button that grounds the side card; B and C each have only some of these, and E has a weak title and a stubby button.

D has the larger bold title, full-width Open calendar button and soft shadows; B has the title but a small button and flat cards; C has button and shadows but a small title; A is flat and small-titled; E has the small button and small title.
